subject: Mathematics
chapterName: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

questions.questionText: A coordinate system acts as a structured framework that enables us to use numbers to describe the exact physical locations of points or objects.
questions.explanationAnswer: This statement is true as it directly matches the definition of a coordinate system provided in the text.
questions.explanationQuestion: The statement tests the basic definition of a coordinate system.

questions.questionText: A system of coordinates is a structured framework that enables us to use ______ to describe the exact physical ______ of points or objects.
questions.explanationAnswer: The definition states that a coordinate system enables us to use 'numbers' to describe the exact physical 'locations' of points or objects.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the missing key terms from the definition of a coordinate system.

questions.questionText: In the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation, city streets were constructed with striking precision in ______ and ______ directions at uniform distances of about $10\text{ metres}$ apart.
questions.explanationAnswer: The text specifies that the streets were constructed in 'North-South' and 'East-West' directions.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the directions in which the streets of the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation were aligned.

questions.questionText: Ptolemy's work on describing latitudes and longitudes built upon earlier works, including that of Hipparchus.
questions.explanationAnswer: This is true. The text explicitly mentions that Ptolemy built on earlier works, 'including that of Hipparchus'.
questions.explanationQuestion: Determine if Ptolemy's work was built upon Hipparchus's earlier contributions.

questions.questionText: The Greek mathematician ______ (c. $150\text{ BCE}$) described the ______ and ______ of thousands of locations, including 'Ozine'.
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states that 'Ptolemy' described the 'latitudes' and 'longitudes' of thousands of locations.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the name of the mathematician and the coordinate terms he described.

questions.questionText: Which ancient location, later identified as Ujjayinī, had its latitude and longitude described by Ptolemy?
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states that Ptolemy described the latitudes and longitudes of thousands of locations, 'including 'Ozine' (Ujjayinī)'.
questions.explanationQuestion: Identify the ancient name used by Ptolemy for Ujjayinī.

questions.questionText: Without Brahmagupta's formalisation of zero and negative numbers, the four-quadrant Cartesian plane would still have been easily developed.
questions.explanationAnswer: This statement is false. The text explicitly states: 'Without Brahmagupta's work, the four-quadrant Cartesian plane, as we will study in this chapter, would be impossible.'
questions.explanationQuestion: Evaluate the necessity of Brahmagupta's work to the development of the Cartesian plane.

questions.questionText: Brahmagupta (c. $628\text{ CE}$) formalised the notion and use of ______ and the ______ numbers as algebraic entities.
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states that Brahmagupta formalised the notion and use of 'zero' and 'negative' numbers.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the mathematical concepts formalised by Brahmagupta.
